class.name: Box3DMotorJoint
class.brief_description: Drives the relative velocity of two bodies, and optionally springs their frames together.
class.description: Two mechanisms in one joint. The velocity half drives the relative linear and angular velocity toward a target within a force and torque budget, like a servo. The spring half (the [code]hertz[/code] properties) pulls the joint frames together instead. The spring half makes an excellent compliant grab handle: Box3D's own samples hold a body at the mouse with [member linear_hertz] around 7.5, [member linear_damping] 1, a force cap, and [member max_torque] as angular friction.

members.member: Stiffness of the rotational spring aligning the joint frames, in cycles per second. 0 disables it.
Target relative angular velocity, in radians per second.
Stiffness of the positional spring pulling the joint frames together, in cycles per second. 0 disables it and leaves only the velocity drive.
Target relative linear velocity, in metres per second.

Force budget for reaching [member linear_velocity], in newtons. Box3D skips the linear velocity drive entirely while this is 0. Defaults to 1000 here rather than Box3D's 0, so the drive works out of the box.

Force budget for the positional spring, in newtons. [b]Box3D runs that spring only while both this and [member linear_hertz] are above 0[/b], and this defaults to 0, so setting the hertz alone does nothing. The scene dock warns about either half being missing.
Torque budget for the rotational spring, in newton-metres. Like [member max_spring_force], the spring runs only while both this and [member angular_hertz] are above 0.

Torque budget for reaching [member angular_velocity], in newton-metres. Doubles as angular friction when [member angular_velocity] is zero. Box3D skips the angular drive entirely while this is 0. Defaults to 1000 here rather than Box3D's 0.
